title: GigaSMART / Advanced Feature Processing Health
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'GigaSMART / Advanced Feature Processing Health' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_gigasmart_advanced_feature_processing_health` (UC-5.17.7), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — GigaSMART / Advanced Feature Processing Health", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=visibility` sourcetype='target_sourcetype' that satisfy the UC-5.17.7 SPL filters for 'GigaSMART / Advanced Feature Processing Health'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `visibility` / `target_sourcetype` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `operational_exceptions.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-5.17.7.

dataSources: Detailed: `index=visibility`; `gigamon:gigasmart`, `gigamon:blade`, `keysight:advanced_apps`, `cpacket:analytics` streaming `feature_state`, `fpga_temp_c`, `sess_table_pct`, `regex_compile_errors`, `ssl_decrypt_failures`. Temperature and memory metrics may arrive via SNMP alongside syslog heartbeats. Collected via Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Gigamon Fabric Manager / REST pollers, Keysight Vision application intelligence exporters, cPacket analytics node syslog; Splunk Supporting Add-on for SNMP for environmental sensors when syslog lacks thermal data. — Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833)
spl:
index=visibility earliest=-8h
| eval v=lower(sourcetype)
| eval vendor=case(match(v,"gigamon"),"Gigamon",match(v,"keysight|ixia|vision"),"Keysight",match(v,"cpacket"),"cPacket","other")
| where vendor!="other"
| eval blade=coalesce(slot_id,module_name,feature_card,"unknown")
| eval healthy=case(match(lower(coalesce(feature_state,svc_status,"")),"up|ok|online|running"),1,tonumber(coalesce(sess_table_pct,table_util_pct))>92,0,tonumber(coalesce(fpga_temp_c,die_temp_c))>85,0,match(_raw,"(?i)(regex.?error|compile.?fail|decrypt.?fail)"),0,1)
| bin _time span=15m
| stats min(healthy) as ok_window max(sess_table_pct) as peak_tbl max(fpga_temp_c) as peak_temp values(feature_state) as states dc(regex_compile_errors) as regex_err by _time vendor host blade
| where ok_window=0 OR peak_tbl>90 OR peak_temp>80 OR regex_err>0
| sort vendor host blade - _time
description: Quarter-hour Splunk health windows combine FPGA-adjacent temperatures, session table saturation, and cryptographic feature errors across Gigamon GigaSMART-class blades and Keysight Vision advanced modules so latent hardware fatigue surfaces before features silently degrade.
value: Platform owners justify proactive blade swaps using Splunk-backed thermal trends while SOC managers avoid unexplained decryption gaps during TLS-heavy incident weeks.
implementation: Maintain vendor-specific temperature thresholds in a lookup by chassis SKU; escalate regex compile failures immediately—these rarely self-heal—while smoothing thermal alarms using rolling medians.
visualization: Small-multiples line charts per blade for peak_temp and peak_tbl; alert table prioritizing regex_err>0; optional geomap only when hosts carry geo metadata.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance** — Planned change generates expected deviations for 'GigaSMART / Advanced Feature Processing Health'. Cross-check change records.

2. **Batch job cycle** — Fixed-schedule workload skews `visibility` metrics.

3. **Monitoring synthetic checks** — Health probes from known hosts.

4. **Onboarding burst** — New entities produce atypical volume until baseline stabilizes.

**Suppression mechanism:** `operational_exceptions.csv` with entity, reason, valid_until.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Hardware BOM noting FPGA-bearing SKUs vs CPU-only analytics blades.
• Environmental baseline (ambient rack temperature, airflow direction).
• Firmware cadence calendar so Splunk suppressions align with reboot-induced spikes.

Step 1 — Instrumentation
Poll REST endpoints exposing session table fills and crypto offload counters; augment with SNMP environmental OIDs where gaps exist.

Step 2 — Parse failures distinctly
Flag TLS handshake failures separately from hardware faults using structured codes—avoid lumping into generic ERROR severity buckets.

Step 3 — Deploy Splunk searches
Save composite SPL `pktbrk_advfeat_health`; acceleration optional via summary indexing due to moderate event volume.

Step 4 — Validate
Stress-test lab appliance until vendor CLI reports table exhaustion—confirm Splunk crosses thresholds simultaneously.

Step 5 — Operationalize
Dashboard overlays thermal curves with HVAC incidents pulled from facility feeds when integrated; attach firmware advisory links in drilldown.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Gigamon Fabric Manager / REST pollers, Keysight Vision application intelligence exporters, cPacket analytics node syslog; Splunk Supporting Add-on for SNMP for environmental sensors when syslog lacks thermal data. — Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into visibility. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`_time, blade, healthy, host`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Some boxes do fancy math on live traffic—unpacking secrets or spotting patterns—and those brains can overheat or fill up like a crowded notebook. We watch those signs so we service the brain before it quietly starts skipping pages.
